tests: Stresses the forecaster's uniform tool-distribution assumption: 10 tools are exposed but ~95% of real calls hit one paid action (stripe.create_charge), so true per-call tool cost is ~10x a per-tool uniform-average estimate.

expected_truth.how_computed: Model claude-sonnet-4-6: input $3.00/MTok = 3.0e-6/tok, output $15.00/MTok = 15.0e-6/tok, cache_discount 0.90, tokenizer_inflation 1.0. llm_per_call = (2200*3.0e-6 + 400*15.0e-6) * (1 - 0.60*0.90) * (1 + 0.04) = (0.0066 + 0.0060) * 0.46 * 1.04 = 0.0126 * 0.46 * 1.04 = 0.006028. tool_per_call = sum(share*unit_cost): 0.95*0.029 = 0.027550, all other actions cost 0.0, so tool_per_call = 0.02755. infra_per_call = 0.001. per_call_total = 0.006028 + 0.02755 + 0.001 = 0.034578. monthly = 120 calls/day * 30 days * 0.034578 = 124.48. monthly_range = 124.48 * [0.85, 1.15] = [105.81, 143.15]. Note: the brief named stripe.create_payout ($0.25), but create_payout is NOT in the spec mockTools stripe action list, so it cannot execute in a sandbox sweep; the most expensive PAID action that exists in BOTH mockTools and toolActionCosts is stripe.create_charge ($0.029), used as the hot tool here to keep the file sweep-executable while preserving the 95/5 skew.
expected_truth.uniform_note: A forecaster that spreads tool cost uniformly across the 10 exposed tools would estimate ~(0.95*0.029)/10 + 0 = ~0.00276-0.0029 per call (the single $0.029 hot cost averaged over all tools), vs the true 0.02755 - roughly a 9.5x underestimate of tool cost.

why_low_tier_will_miss: The LOW tier assumes uniform tool distribution and would amortize the lone paid action across all 10 tools (~$0.0029/call tool cost) plus a static ~100 calls/day, landing near $0.30/call -> ~$30-40/mo on tool spend; convergence to look for is the forecaster's tool_per_call rising ~9.5x to $0.02755 and monthly climbing toward the true ~$124 once it weights tool_call_mix by the observed 95/5 share instead of uniform.

register_payload.name: Skewed Billing Operator
register_payload.description: Adversarial spend-test agent: exposes 10 tools but in practice ~95% of calls hit one expensive paid action (stripe.create_charge). Probes the forecaster's uniform tool-distribution assumption where true tool cost far exceeds a per-tool average estimate.

tools.name: stripe
tools.description: Payments. The hot path: ~95% of real calls create charges (a paid per-call action).

actions.name: create_charge
actions.description: Create a charge against a customer (paid action, $0.029 each). The dominant ~95% of calls.
